svg.title: The mean describes almost nobody
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch of twenty thousand real HTTP latencies drawn as a histogram with a sharp peak at 0.165 milliseconds and a long thin red tail out to 6.876 milliseconds, with dashed lines marking p50, the mean at 0.191, p95, p99 and the maximum, annotated that only 19.8 percent of requests are slower than the mean and that the skewness is 20.56; an SLA on average latency crossed out in red beside an SLA on p99 ticked; four small histograms of sample means at n equal to 1, 5, 30 and 1000 whose skewness falls from 12.90 to 0.62 as the shape becomes symmetric; and a QQ plot whose points bend up away from the diagonal at the right.
svg.text: 20,000 real HTTP latencies, drawn as they actually are
only 19.8% of requests are SLOWER than the mean
p99/p50 = 3.94x · max/p50 = 41.7x · the slowest 1% ate 5.44% of all the time
look at the histogram BEFORE the
everyone passes and users still wait
this one you can actually fail
average n of them, and the shape comes back
the raw data never became normal. The AVERAGE did - and its width
the QQ plot: points bending UP at the right = a heavy tail.
if it were normal they would sit on the dashed line
...so how wide should the interval be? -> Module 3
